propositions: Repeated LLM step call failures (swallowed as abstain/degrade across ~13 sites in src/rebar/llm/) are invisible to verdict consumers because no in-memory counter survives to the final JSON output.
An empty LLM result (e.g., overlap[]) produced by all-calls-failed is byte-identical to one produced by nothing-overlapped, making silent degradation undetectable.

A new run-scoped contextvars sink in step_failures.py records non-fatal failures at the single runner seam (runner.py:573) and drains into coverage.llm_step_failures only when non-empty, keeping clean runs attestation-safe.
coverage.llm_step_failures reports {"total": N, "by_step": {label: count}} where label is the step's _call_label, matching the llm call logs operators would grep.

The sink is activated in plan-review run scope (gate_dispatch) and drained in verdict assembly (workflow_ops), following the established verification_contract_violations posture of present-only-when-nonempty.
No change to any swallow site's behaviour, retry logic, verdict classification, or exit code; every survived failure is by construction already in a run that produced a verdict.
